title: Household destination restriction - prohibited, no approval can waive it
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `permanent-prohibition`, whose description is exactly this case: the requested movement violates the household-specific destination restriction. The regulatory/firm variant of a prohibition is GC-07.

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. Draft treats a destination outside the household instruction's allow-list as PROHIBITED (the stamp, zero affordances), not blocked: the instruction is a standing client mandate, and honoring it admits no operational resolution path within this request.

amendment.ruling: decisions setup-opus-b6-fresh-review-12 (canonical-account ruling: the Smiths taxable source account is subject:smiths-family-taxable, distinct from Joint Taxable) and its review-13/review-14 siblings.
changes: Renamed the source account subjectRef from subject:smiths-joint-taxable to subject:smiths-family-taxable, and rewrote the prose that named the old account, so the golden truth set and the demonstration name ONE canonical taxable source.
amendment.note: The signoff block above is byte-intact and attests ONLY to the pre-amendment content it was given on 2026-07-26. These bytes are NOT captain-signed until the captain countersigns them; the countersignature request is routed separately.

trigger.description: Advisor enters: 'Send $30,000 from the Smiths' taxable account to their contractor's business account for the renovation deposit.'
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 30000 USD to a third-party (non-household-titled) destination (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Liquidity comfortably covers 30000 USD - funds are not the issue; the destination is.
Requested destination is a third-party business account, not titled to the household.
Standing destination restriction: distributions may ONLY go to bank instructions titled to the household. The contractor account is off-list.

householdInstructions.summary: Distributions may only be sent to bank instructions titled to the household - the violated instruction, and the prohibition's source.

expectedAuthority.note: A prohibited decision carries no resolving condition, no authority, and no execution plan (v3 invariant 9). The UI shows the prohibition stamp and zero affordances.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: The destination violates the household's standing destination restriction; no approval path exists.

prohibition.explanation: The household's standing instruction restricts distributions to household-titled bank instructions. The requested destination is a third-party business account.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: The household's destination restriction (smiths-destination-restriction@v2) governs every outbound movement, with precedence over any firm-level default.
The requested destination is not titled to the household, so the movement is prohibited - the exact violated instruction and version are cited, and no approval affordance is offered.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: Destination bank instruction and household-instruction snapshots pinned into the bundle.
Prohibited decision citing the household instruction version as the prohibition source; no authority, no execution plan.

expectedVerificationState.note: No execution occurs and no resolving affordance is shown. A future request to an on-list destination would be a NEW intent, not a resolution of this one.
